summary: Default-enabled, values-controlled static Kubernetes topology-spread constraints for messenger, mail, social, and community FD-001 dogfood tenant workload charts and rendered snapshots.
claim_boundary: This slice adds source-controlled Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints to FD-001 backbone service Helm Deployment templates and static rendered snapshots, with a values-controlled default-enabled switch for target models that need explicit override before live rollout. It proves static chart/snapshot readiness and semantic CI-smoke regression coverage only; it does not claim Kubernetes API admission, live scheduler placement, multi-zone availability, universal self-host portability, ArgoCD sync/health, OpenCost allocation, branch-protection state, remote CI green, or production tenant workload deployment. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the future dogfood substrate/proof point.

best_practice_research.used_for: Grounds use of topology spread constraints to spread Pods across failure domains such as zones and nodes for availability/resource-utilization posture.
Grounds maxSkew, topologyKey, labelSelector, and ScheduleAnyway semantics; ScheduleAnyway is treated as a best-effort skew-reduction preference, not a guarantee.
Keeps this slice scoped to scheduling distribution while recognizing that high availability also needs disruption budgets; existing PDB templates remain separate static evidence.

repo_local_context.use: Existing FD-001 dogfood Deployment templates already carry probes, resources, securityContext, runtimeClassName, tenant/cost labels, and Cosign annotations but lacked topology spread hints.
Static rendered snapshots are the current tenant-cost-label scan target and now mirror topology-spread posture without claiming cluster apply.
Existing backbone CI smoke parses source charts and rendered snapshots; this slice extends required string coverage.

findings: Minimal YAML/static-smoke change; no new controller, generator, runtime dependency, or API surface.
The same two scheduler spread hints are repeated only where Kubernetes workloads consume them: source Helm templates and static rendered snapshots.
FD-001 dogfood workload charts now declare zone and node topology-spread constraints so future scheduler placement can reduce single-failure-domain concentration.
The evidence remains static/source-controlled; it does not claim a live multi-AZ cluster, admitted Pods, or observed scheduler placement.
A RED static check failed before the change because all eight chart/snapshot files lacked topologySpreadConstraints, zone/hostname topology keys, ScheduleAnyway, and maxSkew: 1.
The CI governance smoke now requires these strings for source templates and rendered snapshots to catch future regressions.
Uses standard Kubernetes pod spec topologySpreadConstraints with existing app.kubernetes.io/name selector labels; no custom abstraction for operators to learn.
The template and rendered snapshot shapes stay parseable YAML/Helm text and preserve existing probe/resource/security/non-claim checks.

Chose ScheduleAnyway constraints instead of DoNotSchedule/minDomains because this slice is a best-effort placement-preference contract for FD-001 dogfood charts, not a hard availability or universal portability guarantee.

The static charts assume target nodes expose the selected topology labels when operators want zone/hostname spreading; clusters with different label topology need explicit chart-policy follow-up rather than relying on this slice as proof of portability.
Did not add pod anti-affinity because topology spread expresses both node and zone failure-domain hints with less brittle scheduling behavior for the future Oyatie Cloud dogfood substrate.
No secret, credential, network policy, RBAC, auth, or container-permission changes are introduced. Existing restricted-style pod security contexts remain intact.

ScheduleAnyway is treated here as a soft scheduler preference to reduce skew when the configured topology keys are available; this static slice does not claim live scheduler behavior for clusters with missing topology labels. No runtime hot path changes.
Maintains FD-001 tenant/cost/regulatory labels and explicit non-claim annotations on rendered snapshots; no live OpenCost or admission evidence is asserted.
Rollback is deleting the topologySpreadConstraints blocks and removing the CI required strings/evidence arg; no data or API migration.
The change strengthens static workload shape that future telemetry can correlate with topology/failure-domain placement, but emits no live telemetry itself.
No public API/schema compatibility impact.

Kubernetes portability is not claimed here: the source templates now carry values-controlled, default-enabled zone/hostname spread hints for the FD-001 dogfood posture, and deployment models with different node-label conventions need an explicit chart override/validation slice before live rollout.
Uses existing CS-BACKBONE slice naming and no new crates/packages.
Updates active task plan/todo and evidence only; no new root Markdown or retired path.
Keeps source Helm templates under microservices/*/iac/k8s/helm and static snapshots under existing iac/helm/oyatie-cloud-dogfood/rendered.
Infrastructure contract change only; no domain/app adapter boundary drift.
No dependency changes.
No schema or algorithm changes.
Backbone governance smoke now blocks topology-spread regression for all four FD-001 dogfood workload charts and snapshots.
